fact: Since 3 August 2026 Congolese taxpayers can pay taxes, levies and customs duties online through the Fouta national switch after filing on the E-Tax or Sydonia platforms, with an electronic Treasury receipt issued, according to L'Economie.
The Fouta pilot with firms already used to e-filing is complete and rollout is progressive, to large then medium companies and to all taxpayers by the end of 2026, according to L'Economie.

Arrete no. 1009 of 22 May 2026 makes payment of public revenue exclusively electronic through the FOUTA platform, described as a national switch for tax and customs collection, with a 60-day compliance period.
The arrete says FOUTA applies to all public revenue including taxes, duties and fees, and is the single payment channel for tax and customs levies credited to the Treasury account at the BEAC.
The Treasury sheet says transactional platforms built with the mobile operators allow paperless payment of utility bills and, most recently, of land transport taxes.

Congo's finance ministry demonstrated Fouta to the Assembly finance committee on 23 June 2026, with real tax and customs e-filing and e-payment operations via Banque postale, BGFI and BOA and an emailed receipt, but the document does not say it is in service.
MTN Congo's page says taxpayers fill in their tax declaration on impots.gouv.cg and pay e-tax and e-douane bills by MTN Mobile Money, free of charge, from 1 to 750,000 FCFA.

ACSI's director general told the National Assembly's Ecofin committee on 17 November 2026 that the single service-revenue till and the dematerialised local-authority revenue platform, entrusted to ACSI under the 2025 and 2026 finance laws, are ready to go into production during 2027.

fact: Minister Christian Yoka said the Fouta platform collected 107 billion FCFA from its launch on 1 June to 16 November 2026, through seven banks.
The ministry says 94 billion FCFA came from taxes through the e-Tax online filing and payment system and 13 billion from duties and taxes through Sydonia customs.
The ministry says revenue collected through Fouta equals 8.5% of 2026 tax revenue, 107 billion FCFA by 16 November.
Finance minister Christian Yoka told the National Assembly that the FOUTA platform, launched on 1 June 2026, collects public revenue through seven named banks, with MUCODEC and UBA to join.
Yoka said FOUTA is the single payment and collection channel for customs revenue through SYDONIA and tax revenue through e-Tax, as well as forestry, oil, administrative and domain revenue.
Yoka said FOUTA had collected nearly FCFA 107 billion by 16 November 2026, FCFA 94 billion through e-Tax and FCFA 13 billion through SYDONIA, against about FCFA 1 billion for its predecessor e-Pay.
